question:
If the area of the base of a right circular cone is 157 cm² and its slant height is sqrt{491} cm, then the volume of the cone is _______.

(Use π = 3.14.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given Base Area = 157 cm², so π × r² = 157 ⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50.

Height h = √(l² − r²) = √(491 − 50) = √441 = 21 cm.

Volume of cone = (1/3) × Base Area × Height.

Volume = (1/3) × 157 × 21 = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base area of the cone = 157 cm²

Slant height (l) = √491 cm

(π = 3.14)

**Formula Used:**

Area of base = π × r²

Slant height l = √(r² + h²)

Volume of a cone V = 1/3 × π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d8215c8fcfdba95cdc1404e58bb7c24c778affb28542bf6bddbd1199195ea4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of base = π × r² = 157

⇒ 3.14 × r² = 157

⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50

⇒ We know that, l² = r² + h²

⇒ (√491)² = 50 + h²

⇒ 491 = 50 + h²

⇒ h² = 491 − 50 = 441

⇒ h = √441 = 21 cm

⇒ Volume of the cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h

⇒ Volume = 1/3 × (3.14 × 50) × 21

⇒ Volume = 1/3 × 157 × 21

⇒ Volume = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone vs Cylinder

A cone's volume is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height. The formula is V = 1/3 × πr²h.

Surface Area of a Cone

The curved surface area is given by πrl and the total surface area is given by πr(r + l), where r is the radius and l is the slant height.

Frustum of a Cone

When a cone is sliced parallel to its base, the remaining lower part is called a frustum. Its volume is 1/3 × πh(R² + r² + Rr).
